claims.text: Greer founded CSETI in 1990 and the Disclosure Project in 1993; the Disclosure Project seeks amnesty for government whistleblowers willing to violate security oaths.

claimsMade.text: On why the craft is described with no windows: a 'synthetic vision system [used] the same kind of technology as the gun slaving system they have in the Apache helicopter', with paired slewing cameras and 'a little screen in front of his helmet', giving 'a perfect 3-D view of the outside, but no windows'.

On the crew compartment and the central column: the visible dome 'was actually the upper half of a big sphere-shaped crew compartment that was in the middle of the vehicle'; 'On the inside of the crew compartment was a big column that ran down through the middle, and there were four ejection seats mounted back-to-back on the upper half of this column. Then, right in the middle of the column, was a large flywheel of some kind.'

connections.label: Central Intelligence Agency
connections.note: CSETI founder Steven Greer says he briefed sitting CIA Director R. James Woolsey on UFOs on 13 December 1993 at a dinner in Arlington arranged by John Petersen, and quotes a Petersen memo referring to sabotage of 'Project Starlight', the CSETI disclosure effort. Woolsey and the other attendees disputed this characterisation in a signed 16 September 1999 letter, saying it was a dinner party and that Greer's published account was distorted. Both accounts are on the record; the relationship is contested.

desc: The Center for the Study of Extraterrestrial Intelligence, founded by Steven Greer in 1990, and the Disclosure Project, founded by him in 1993, are the originating institutions of the whistleblower-aggregation model: collect insiders, give them a platform, argue for amnesty for those who break their oaths. The May 2001 National Press Club event with twenty retired Air Force, FAA and intelligence officers established the format that every subsequent disclosure press conference has copied, including Greer's own 8 May 2026 event. The organisations' evidentiary record is poor - the Atacama skeleton presented in Sirius was shown genetically to be human - and the newer structural investigators define themselves explicitly against this model.
